title: «Bismillah» and «Alhamdulillah»: Tying the Whole Day to Allah
summary: A two-year-old learns by routine, not by explanation. So tie the two phrases to two fixed moments he already knows: «Bismillah» before eating and «Alhamdulillah» after. Say them yourself every time even if he does not speak, because a child imitates what he sees consistently, not what he is told to do. After a few weeks you will find him saying it before you do — and that is the first time he remembers Allah of his own accord.
try_this: This week: pick one fixed daily meal and say «Bismillah» before it and «Alhamdulillah» after it out loud. One meal is enough.
reflection_prompts: Which moment in your day recurs without exception and suits anchoring these two phrases?
Does your child hear you say it to yourself, or only when you are directing him?

review_defects.arabic: أي لحظةٍ في يومكما تتكرّر بلا استثناء وتصلح لتثبيت الكلمتين؟
review_defects.english: Which moment in your day recurs without exception and suits anchoring these two phrases?
review_defects.why: The Arabic uses the dual form 'يومكما' (the day of you both, i.e., mother and child), emphasizing a shared routine. The English 'your day' could be read as referring only to the mother's day, losing the dual nuance.
